lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.20 - A Look & learn

details: Look & learn helps students recognise key vocabulary and sentence structures by providing examples of positive and negative imperatives and preparing them for writing and speaking activities.
Look for good understanding of the grammar shown in the table and evidence of understanding key structures.

“Remember! It’s very important to follow the rules in different countries. Can you think of some rules here? When I’m on holiday, I am always polite! And I’m never rude. Can you help me practise correct sentences for instructions? Let’s be nice and make friends on holiday!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.20 - B. Tick the imperative sentences

details: Tick the imperative sentences helps consolidate learning by asking students to recognise the imperative in example sentences, practising careful reading.
Look for accurate answers, a good understanding of the imperative and neat work.
“Oh dear. I just don’t know! Can you help me work out which of these sentences tell someone what to do? When you do, you can give them a tick.”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.20 - C. Match the sentences

details: Match the sentences helps students recognise cause and effect by matching sentence halves, practising reading comprehension, grammar structures, and making connections between ideas.
Look for correct matches, careful reading and a clear understanding of sentence meaning.
“It’s so hot in here! I might take off my coat. Some sentences tell you what to do. Let’s read and match each one so they make sense. Ready?!”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.20 - D. Correct the underlined words and rewrite the sentences.

details: Correct the underlined words and rewrite the sentences helps students practice spelling, grammar and accuracy by identifying mistakes and correcting them by rewriting the sentences.
Look for accurate corrections, spelling and grammar and careful attention to detail.
“Uh oh! Some mistakes have snuck into my sentences. Can you be a sentence detective and find them all? Please help me fix them. Can you think of any more important rules to remember?”
